GRR.headline: Flood Watch continues along I-94 corridor tonight into Sunday

areas.label: Heavy rain, flooding on saturated ground
areas.quote: High resolution models show the low level jet aimed at our far southern CWA towards I-94. This should be the focus area for heavy rain tonight based on the moisture transport vectors centered in that area as well.

areas.label: Waves 3-5 ft north of Whitehall
areas.quote: There is an indication however that waves may push into the 3 to 5 foot range Sunday into Monday, especially from Whitehall north up the shoreline.

DTX.headline: Heavy rain and dense fog tonight south of M-59; showers exit Sunday

areas.label: Training showers, 1+ inch rain
areas.quote: Additional showers are expected overnight, some of which will be capable of producing heavy rainfall, more so for areas south of M-59 where potential exists for training/repeated showers.

areas.label: Locally dense overnight fog
areas.quote: Potential exists for locally dense patches at times, therefore, a Dense Fog Advisory may be needed on short notice.

areas.label: Small Craft Advisory nearshore
areas.quote: While gales currently look unlikely, onshore flow warrants long duration Small Craft Advisories for all nearshore waters.

APX.headline: Cool and mostly dry; light showers south of M-72 tonight, patchy frost Monday night

areas.label: A few light showers south of M-72
areas.quote:
A few showers over northern lower tonight, more numerous 
  south of M-72.

areas.label: Patchy frost in interior areas
areas.quote:
Monday will 
be the coolest day with highs in the mid 50s to lower 60s, 
setting us up for a very cool and possibly frosty night in at 
least some interior areas (if the winds decouple).

areas.label: Small Craft Advisory on the lakes
areas.quote:
Small Craft Advisory from 2 PM Sunday to 8 PM EDT Monday for 
     LHZ348-349.

MQT.headline: Lake-enhanced showers and hazardous Lake Superior swimming Sunday

areas.label: 6 ft waves, rip current risk
areas.quote: This in turn cranks wave heights up to 6 ft within 5 miles of the Lake Superior shoreline, which will drastically increase the risk of hazardous rip currents and challenging swimming conditions for those trying to squeeze in a late-September Sunday beach day at Lake Superior beaches.

areas.label: Lake-enhanced showers, W/NC UP
areas.quote:
Light lake-enhanced showers will be possible (30-50%) especially 
along the terrain of the western and north-central UP Sunday.

areas.label: Morning frost potential
areas.quote:
Below-average temperatures expected through Wednesday (including 
morning frost potential), giving way to above-normal temperatures 
late week.
